prompt: An unloaded divider has equal upper and lower resistors across a fixed supply. You increase only the upper resistor. What happens to the junction voltage measured from ground?

options.text: It stays halfway because there are still two resistors
options.explanation: Half the voltage requires equal resistances, not merely two components.
A larger upper resistor takes a larger share of the supply drop, leaving less across the lower resistor.
Correct. The lower resistor now represents a smaller share of total resistance.
This passive divider cannot create a voltage above its positive supply in the stated circuit.

workedExample: The unloaded series current flows through both resistors. Raising the upper resistance makes it take more of the voltage drop. The junction voltage is the lower resistor’s drop, so it falls. Check which resistor is connected to ground before making the prediction.
